modules.name: AngularJS client-side template / expression injection
modules.description: Finds AngularJS code patterns where untrusted data is compiled or parsed as AngularJS expressions/templates, including $parse, $interpolate, $compile, interpolation delimiters and ng-* expression attributes.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid passing user-controlled strings to AngularJS expression or template compilation APIs. Do not server-render user input inside {{...}}, [[...]], ng-* expression attributes, or $parse/$compile/$interpolate inputs. Use text-only rendering, strict allow-lists for expression name

modules.name: Client Script Loader Poisoning
modules.description: Detects dynamic script, worker, and service-worker loader endpoints that can be influenced by attacker-controlled client-side data.
modules.recommendationSummary: Load workers, service workers, and helper scripts from fixed, trusted URLs only. Do not derive script loader destinations from URL parameters, storage, messages, or DOM input. Apply strict allow-lists for scheme, host, and path before invoking worker or script loader APIs.

modules.name: Client-side Template Injection
modules.description: Detects dynamic client-side template compilation/rendering where attacker-controlled templates or outputs are injected into the DOM.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid compiling templates from untrusted strings; use precompiled templates. Sanitize render output before inserting into the DOM.

modules.name: DOM-based Cookie Manipulation
modules.description: Detects cases where attacker-controlled DOM data is written into cookies (document.cookie or common wrapper functions). Can indicate session fixation, logic control, or preparation for exploit-chains.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid writing security-sensitive cookies from untrusted client-side data. Prefer server-side cookie setting and validation. For non-security cookies, validate/allow-list values, and avoid storing secrets client-side. Use HttpOnly for session cookies.

modules.name: DOM Data Manipulation
modules.description: Detects untrusted DOM data being written into form metadata (formAction/target/method/value/placeholder), inline style surfaces (style/cssText/background*), document.title, history state, or createHTMLDocument — mutations that influence UI/navigation state without covering classic href/src/action sinks already handled elsewhere.
modules.recommendationSummary: Validate or allow-list values before assigning them to form metadata, placeholders, or styles. Prefer safe DOM APIs (textContent, dataset) when representing user data. Keep document.title and history.pushState/replaceState inputs confined to trusted sources; normalise or encode u

modules.name: DOM-based XSS
modules.description: Detects cases where untrusted data from the DOM (URL, element values, storage, messages, etc.) flows into HTML/JS execution sinks (e.g., innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write, string-based setTimeout, insertAdjacentHTML) without proper sanitization or encoding \u2014 enabling DOM-based cross-site scripting.
modules.recommendationSummary: Prevent DOM-based XSS by never inserting untrusted strings directly into HTML or executing them as code. Prefer DOM/text APIs, safe templating, or a vetted sanitizer and apply context-aware encoding where needed. Primary: Use textContent / innerText or create DOM nodes instead of

modules.name: DOM-based JavaScript Injection
modules.description: Detects dynamic execution of attacker-controlled strings in JavaScript sinks such as eval(), Function(), string-based timers, execScript, or script.text assignments. Exploiting these flows lets attackers execute arbitrary JS without relying on HTML injection.
modules.recommendationSummary: Never pass untrusted strings to dynamic code execution APIs (eval, Function, string-based setTimeout/setInterval, execScript). Prefer callbacks and safe parsers: pass actual functions to timers and use JSON.parse or allow-lists for data-driven logic. Sanitize and validate any dat

modules.name: DOM-based Link Manipulation
modules.description: Detects DOM code that rewrites link destinations (href attributes) with attacker-controlled data. Manipulated links can mislead users into visiting malicious targets even if navigation is not forced automatically.
modules.recommendationSummary: Allow-list link destinations or map tokens to server-side known URLs; do not reflect arbitrary strings into href attributes. Ensure displayed link text matches the trusted destination so users cannot be tricked into clicking a mismatched URL. Sanitise or normalise protocol and ho

modules.name: Network Destination Poisoning
modules.description: Detects client-side request destinations for beacon, EventSource, and Axios that can be influenced by attacker-controlled input.
modules.recommendationSummary: Build beacon, EventSource, and API client destinations from fixed configuration, not user-controlled strings. Apply strict allow-lists for scheme, host, and path before constructing network destinations. Reject attacker-controlled cross-origin URLs even when requests are “read-on

modules.name: Open Redirection
modules.description: Detects client-side code that can redirect users to attacker-controlled URLs (open redirects). Includes assignment/calls that control window/location/navigation, attr-based redirects, form actions and jQuery variants.
modules.recommendationSummary: Prevent open redirects by validating or allow-listing redirect targets, rejecting external or absolute URLs from untrusted sources, and mapping user inputs to predefined safe destinations instead of using them directly in navigation APIs.

modules.name: Web Message Handling
modules.description: Detects unsafe postMessage usage and message event handling issues (missing origin validation, wildcard targetOrigin, tainted data flowing into DOM/code sinks).
modules.recommendationSummary: Always specify an exact targetOrigin and validate event.origin against a strict allow-list (exact match) before trusting event.data. Sanitize or validate structured payloads before invoking DOM APIs or dynamic execution sinks. Avoid propagating messages into navigation, cookie, o

modules.name: Ajax Request Header Manipulation
modules.description: Detects untrusted data flowing into XMLHttpRequest headers, open/send parameters, and related eval helpers for Ajax requests.
modules.recommendationSummary: Whitelist header names and validate values before invoking setRequestHeader or building fetch headers. Avoid copying sensitive data (cookies, auth tokens) into request headers client-side. Sanitize message payloads and enforce strict origin checks when constructing headers from p

modules.name: Browser Privileged Surface Discovery
modules.description: Identifies browser and service-worker APIs that often gate privileged workflows and deserve explicit review during bug bounty triage.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory every privileged browser API usage and confirm the surrounding workflow enforces authentication and authorization. Review service-worker lifecycle, push, and sync handlers for hidden routes, offline-only actions, and admin-only capabilities. Validate destination URLs an

modules.name: Client-side JSON / SQL / XPath Injection
modules.description: Detects client-side SQL, XPath, and JSON misuse (string concatenation, eval of JSON, XPath without escaping) that can be influenced by untrusted input.
modules.recommendationSummary: Never concatenate untrusted data into SQL or XPath expressions. Use parameterized queries and escape helpers. Avoid eval for JSON parsing — prefer JSON.parse followed by strict type checks. Escape XPath fragments with a dedicated helper (e.g., escapeXPath).

modules.name: Client-side Regex DoS
modules.description: Detects dynamic regular-expression construction from untrusted data that can trigger catastrophic backtracking.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid creating regular expressions directly from attacker-controlled input. Use strict allow-lists for accepted patterns and enforce length/complexity limits. Prefer safe parsing strategies for user-provided filters.

modules.name: Cross-context Channel Discovery
modules.description: Identifies BroadcastChannel and MessageChannel surfaces that should be reviewed as cross-tab or cross-context trust boundaries.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory channel names and message schemas for every BroadcastChannel and MessageChannel usage. Do not assume same-origin browser contexts are equally trusted; validate message payloads and privilege boundaries explicitly. Review privileged workflows triggered from channel messa

modules.name: Document Domain Manipulation
modules.description: Detects direct or tainted assignments to document.domain that can weaken same-origin isolation.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid using document.domain relaxation where possible; prefer explicit cross-origin communication channels. Never derive domain values from URL parameters, storage, or message payloads. If unavoidable, enforce a strict, static allow-list and validate exact host values.

modules.name: DOM Clobbering
modules.description: Detects DOM clobbering risks where attacker-controlled HTML or attributes create id/name collisions (e.g., form/iframe names, global ids) that shadow trusted globals or properties.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid injecting attacker-controlled HTML that includes id/name attributes. Build elements with safe DOM APIs and strict allow-lists. Sanitize dynamic HTML before insertion and prefer textContent when possible. Validate or normalise id/name attributes to avoid collisions with glob

modules.name: DOM Local File Path Manipulation
modules.description: Detects untrusted values flowing into FileReader read methods and local file processing paths.
modules.recommendationSummary: Only read user-selected files from trusted input elements and validated workflows. Do not let URL or message data choose local file objects for processing. Validate file source/context before read operations.

modules.name: DOM Selector Injection
modules.description: Detects CSS selector injection risks where untrusted data controls query selectors (document.querySelector / jQuery) and related origin checks.
modules.recommendationSummary: Never build selectors directly from user input. Validate against strict allow-lists or escape with CSS.escape. For cross-window messaging, verify event.origin with strict equality and validate structured payloads before using selector strings. Avoid wildcard postMessage target or

modules.name: GraphQL Client Discovery
modules.description: Identifies static GraphQL client endpoints and constructors so they can be triaged as attack-surface hints.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory GraphQL endpoints, transports, and client libraries used by the application. Review every discovered query, mutation, and subscription path for authz, IDOR, and introspection issues. Prefer persisted operations and server-side authorization checks for sensitive GraphQL

modules.name: Internal Host and Environment Discovery
modules.description: Identifies internal, localhost, RFC1918, and non-production destinations embedded in client code.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory non-production, internal, and privileged hosts referenced by the client. Review whether these destinations remain reachable from untrusted user contexts. Treat hardcoded environment hosts as candidate pivot points, not as harmless operational leftovers.

modules.name: JWT Client Misuse
modules.description: Detects unsafe handling of JWTs on the client (extraction from URL fragments, insecure storage, appending to URLs/headers).
modules.recommendationSummary: Do not read tokens from URL fragments/query params or store them in Web Storage. Use HttpOnly cookies and avoid reflecting tokens into URLs/headers from untrusted sources. Validate tokens server-side only.

modules.name: Markdown and Rich Content Rendering
modules.description: Detects markdown-to-HTML renderers and taint flows where untrusted markdown is rendered into DOM HTML sinks.
modules.recommendationSummary: Treat markdown and rich-text rendering as HTML generation, not plain text. Disable raw HTML where possible and sanitize rendered output before inserting it into DOM sinks. Prefer allow-listed markdown features and test renderer options for XSS bypasses.

modules.name: OAuth and OIDC Client Flow Discovery
modules.description: Identifies OAuth and OIDC endpoints, protocol parameters, and weak client-side persistence that are valuable during authz and redirect testing.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory authorize, token, logout, and callback flows from client code. Review how redirect_uri, state, nonce, and PKCE values are built and persisted. Do not trust client-side storage or navigation guards as the real OAuth/OIDC security boundary.

modules.name: Client-side Prototype Pollution
modules.description: Detects prototype manipulation in client-side code (assigning __proto__, Object.setPrototypeOf, Object.assign on Object.prototype) that can lead to arbitrary property injection.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid writing to __proto__ or mutating Object.prototype. Clone inputs defensively and validate object shapes before merging.

modules.name: Proxy Override Header Poisoning
modules.description: Detects dangerous request-header overrides that can influence routing, method handling, or upstream authorization logic.
modules.recommendationSummary: Do not build proxy or routing override headers from untrusted client input. Review every use of X-Original-URL, X-Forwarded-*, and method override headers against the upstream proxy chain. Enforce trusted-header policies server-side; never rely on the browser as a safe origin for

modules.name: Real-time Transport Poisoning
modules.description: Detects dynamic client-side transport endpoints and real-time communication primitives such as WebTransport and RTCPeerConnection that should be inventoried during bug bounty triage.
modules.recommendationSummary: Build transport destinations from fixed configuration and strict allow-lists, not user-controlled strings. Inventory every real-time transport surface and review authentication, authorization, and tenant isolation assumptions. Treat browser-native transport constructors as privil

modules.name: SAML SSO Client Flow Discovery
modules.description: Identifies SAML bootstrap routes, protocol parameters, and RelayState handling that are useful during authz and redirect testing.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory SAML login, ACS, and SSO bootstrap paths visible to the client. Review how RelayState is read, written, and persisted. Treat client-side SAML routing helpers as attack-surface hints, not as real authorization controls.

modules.name: Secrets & Credentials Exposure
modules.description: Detects hardcoded secrets across comments, strings, declarations, and headers (API keys, access tokens, private keys, webhooks, auth headers, and common cloud/provider credentials).
modules.recommendationSummary: Remove secrets from code and comments immediately; rotate exposed credentials. Use a secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault); inject at runtime via environment or secure config. Enable CI/CD secret scanning and pre-commit hooks; add server

modules.name: Service Worker Cache Poisoning
modules.description: Detects risky fetch handlers and cache/redirect logic in Service Workers that trust request URLs.
modules.recommendationSummary: Validate and restrict event.request.url before cache writes or redirects. Map allowed paths explicitly and avoid wildcard cache keys.

modules.name: Storage Security
modules.description: Detects sensitive data stored in localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB and tainted data persisted client-side.
modules.recommendationSummary: Avoid storing secrets or tokens in Web Storage/IndexedDB; prefer HttpOnly cookies or server-side session. Validate keys/values and encrypt/expire where unavoidable.

modules.name: Trusted Types Policy Review
modules.description: Identifies Trusted Types policy creation points that should be reviewed as code-execution or DOM-injection trust boundaries.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory every Trusted Types policy and document exactly which sinks it is intended to protect. Avoid permissive default policies that silently allow unsafe HTML, script, or script-URL creation. Review policy callbacks as privileged code because they often become the final bypas

modules.name: Upload and Object Storage Discovery
modules.description: Identifies upload-capable code paths, pre-signed storage URLs, and cloud object destinations that deserve explicit attack-surface review.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory every upload and object-storage destination exposed by the client. Review signed URL generation, content-type enforcement, overwrite rules, and bucket ACL assumptions. Validate file metadata and authorization on the server even when the client appears constrained.

modules.name: WebAuthn and Passkey Discovery
modules.description: Identifies WebAuthn and passkey entry points that should be reviewed as privileged authentication surfaces.
modules.recommendationSummary: Inventory every passkey registration and authentication path exposed to the browser. Review registration, challenge fetching, and conditional mediation flows for hidden auth assumptions. Treat WebAuthn helpers as auth-flow surfaces that deserve explicit authorization and UX revie

modules.name: WebSocket URL Poisoning
modules.description: Detects dynamic WebSocket endpoint selection from untrusted client-side data.
modules.recommendationSummary: Build WebSocket endpoints from fixed configuration, not user-controlled values. Allow-list exact protocols/hosts/paths before constructing WebSocket URLs. Reject or normalize untrusted scheme/host components.
